content.user_title: Build Conversation Memory for AI Assistants
content.value_statement: LLM assistants lose useful context when conversations span sessions or topics. This skill shows practical memory patterns for storage, retrieval, consolidation, and user isolation.
actual_capabilities: Explains tiered memory with buffer, short-term, long-term, and entity stores.
Shows how to extract and update entity facts from conversation messages.
Demonstrates prompt construction with relevant memories and recent context.
Covers importance scoring, consolidation, cleanup, and storage limits.
Describes user isolation, ownership checks, export, and deletion workflows.
Lists validation checks for privacy, retrieval, cleanup, and memory growth issues.
limitations: Provides patterns and examples, not a complete production package.
Assumes existing LLM, memory store, and semantic search abstractions.
Does not cover database administration or knowledge graph construction.
Requires application-specific privacy review before storing user data.

use_cases.title: Add Memory to an Assistant
use_cases.description: Design memory tiers that keep recent chat context while preserving important long-term facts across sessions.

use_cases.title: Control Memory Growth
use_cases.description: Apply scoring, limits, consolidation, and cleanup so memory storage remains useful and cost aware.

use_cases.title: Review Memory Privacy
use_cases.description: Check user isolation, ownership verification, export, deletion, and retrieval filters before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Memory Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a simple conversation memory layer for my assistant. Include short-term memory, long-term memory, and entity memory.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Memory Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current memory retrieval approach. Suggest relevance scoring, result limits, and context formatting improvements for better answers.

prompt_templates.title: Add Privacy Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my memory design for user isolation, deletion, export, and ownership checks. List gaps and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Memory Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production memory architecture for a multi-user LLM app. Include storage tiers, consolidation, cleanup, retrieval, and privacy boundaries.

output_examples.input: Design memory for a customer support assistant that remembers preferences and unresolved issues.
output_examples.output: A three-tier memory plan with recent session context, persistent customer facts, issue history, cleanup rules, and user-specific retrieval filters.

output_examples.input: Audit my assistant because users may see memories from other accounts.
output_examples.output: A privacy checklist covering user-scoped keys, mandatory retrieval filters, ownership checks, access-denied handling, and user data deletion.

output_examples.input: My memory store is growing too fast and retrieval quality is declining.
output_examples.output: A lifecycle plan with importance scoring, short-term limits, consolidation thresholds, low-value memory deletion, and relevance reranking.

best_practices: Store only useful memories after scoring importance and privacy impact.
Filter every memory operation by authenticated user identity.
Keep retrieval results small, relevant, and clearly separated from current user input.
anti_patterns: Do not store every message as long-term memory without cleanup.
Do not share memory namespaces across users or tenants.
Do not include irrelevant memories in prompts just because they match keywords.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design persistent conversation memory for LLM applications, including tiers, retrieval, consolidation, and privacy controls.

faq.question: Is this a ready-to-run memory library?
faq.answer: No. It is an implementation guide with patterns and examples that you adapt to your application stack.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover multi-user privacy?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes user-scoped storage keys, retrieval filters, ownership checks, export, and deletion.

faq.question: Does it solve semantic search for me?
faq.answer: No. It assumes you have a memory store and search method, then shows how to use them safely.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the task does not involve conversation memory, persistent context, or chat history design.
